temporal.gui.title: Temporal
temporal.gui.why.fsrOnly: Only FSR 1, FSR 3 and NIS sharpen.
temporal.gui.why.ownAntiAliasing: DLSS and FSR 3 anti-alias on their own.
temporal.gui.why.windowsOnly: DLSS, FSR 3 and frame generation only work on Windows. FSR 1 and TAA work everywhere.
temporal.gui.narration.usage: Use the left and right arrow keys to change it
temporal.configuration.title: Temporal Settings
temporal.configuration.enabled.tooltip: Render the world at a reduced resolution and upscale it. The HUD always stays at full resolution.
temporal.configuration.renderScale.toolt: Fraction of the window resolution the world is rendered at. Lower = faster but softer. 1.0 = native.
temporal.configuration.upscaler.tooltip:
FSR 1: edge-aware upscale plus sharpening, uses Render Scale and Anti-Aliasing. Works on any GPU.
FSR 3: AMD's temporal upscaler and anti-aliasing. Works on most GPUs.
DLSS: NVIDIA's upscaler and anti-aliasing (RTX GPUs).
NIS: NVIDIA Image Scaling, a sharp edge-aware upscale up to 2x (Render Scale 50% or more), uses Render Scale and Anti-Aliasing. Works on any GPU except on macOS.
FSR 3 and DLSS use Quality Mode instead of Render Scale and Anti-Aliasing.
Bilinear: plain smooth stretch.
Nearest: blocky pixels.
temporal.configuration.qualityMode.toolt:
Used by FSR 3 and DLSS.
Native: full resolution, anti-aliasing only (DLAA / FSR Native AA).
Quality: 67% resolution. Balanced: 58-59%. Performance: 50%. Ultra Performance: 33%.
temporal.configuration.sharpness.tooltip:
Sharpening strength. 0 = off.
FSR 1, FSR 3 and NIS sharpen as they upscale.
DLSS has no sharpening of its own: here NVIDIA Image Scaling sharpens the result. It has its own value, off unless you raise it.
temporal.configuration.antiAliasing.tool:
TAA: smooths jagged edges and shimmering by blending recent frames. Fast-moving mobs may leave a faint trail.
Off: no anti-aliasing.
temporal.configuration.dlssModel.tooltip:
Which DLSS model upscales the image (DLSS only).
Automatic: NVIDIA's pick for each Quality Mode (Transformer K, M or L).
Transformer K: best overall quality.
Transformer L: sharpest and steadiest, the slowest.
Transformer M: close to L, a bit faster.
Transformer J: a little less ghosting, a little more flicker.
CNN: the older, lighter model.
temporal.configuration.frameGeneration.t:
Adds generated frames between rendered ones for smoother motion.
DLSS: RTX 40 or newer (3x-6x: RTX 50).
FSR 3: most GPUs, up to 2x.
With V-Sync on, it's capped at your monitor's refresh rate.
temporal.configuration.frameGenerationMe:
Automatic: DLSS Frame Generation on NVIDIA RTX 40 and newer GPUs, AMD FSR 3 on every other GPU.
DLSS: always DLSS Frame Generation (RTX 40 or newer).
FSR 3: always AMD FSR 3 Frame Generation (up to 2x).
temporal.configuration.dynamicResolution:
The frame rate to hold. When your graphics card can't keep up, the render resolution drops (down to 50%) and comes back when there's room. Render Scale, or with DLSS and FSR 3 the Quality Mode, is the highest it goes.
It watches how long the graphics card takes, so when something else slows the game (the CPU, a big modpack) it leaves the picture alone.
Counts rendered frames, before frame generation.
Off: the resolution stays at Render Scale.
temporal.gui.why.qualityMode: DLSS and FSR 3 use Quality Mode instead.
temporal.configuration.fpsCounter.toolti:
Shows your frame rate in the top-left corner.
With frame generation it counts the frames that reach your screen, with the rendered frames in brackets. Minecraft's own counter only counts rendered frames.
temporal.frameGeneration.limited: Temporal: this GPU can generate up to %sx, so Frame Generation uses that.
temporal.frameGeneration.limitedFsr: Temporal: FSR 3 Frame Generation goes up to 2x, so it uses that.
